answer: To field 100 fakes, an attacker must first produce 100 licensed surveyors. Each licence takes a two-year apprenticeship, an exam and a field test; its certificate bears a velvet-thread watermark, and one seal backs one identity. Surveys go in a spiral-bound field book countersigned by the client, so borrowed work fails audit. Each fake costs 900 units plus 730 days, so 100 fakes cost 90,000 units and 200 surveyor-years. The cheapest cheat is buying a retired surveyor's licence for 2,500 units; the seller gives up their own seal, and a forgery fails the registry cipher check.
